description: The bar chart illustrates the number of datasets published per year from 2012 to 2022, categorized by the number of data sources used: “1” (single source, shown in blue) and “2+” (multiple sources, shown in orange), as part of a systematic review on hateful communication datasets. The vertical axis, labeled “Number of datasets,” ranges from 0 to 100 in increments of 20, while the horizontal axis displays years from 2012 to 2022. Dataset counts are minimal in early years — for example, 2012 and 2013 each show 1–2 datasets, mostly from single sources. A gradual increase begins in 2016, with 10 datasets (8 from single sources, 2 from multiple). Growth accelerates through 2018–2020: 2018 has 30 total (18 single, 12 multiple), 2019 has 45 (25 single, 20 multiple), and 2020 peaks at 128 total (85 single, 43 multiple). In 2021, the count drops to 75 (45 single, 30 multiple), and in 2022, it further declines to 30 total (25 single, 5 multiple), with the 2022 bars shaded light gray, possibly indicating incomplete or provisional data. The chart visually emphasizes the surge in dataset creation around 2020, with single-source datasets consistently outnumbering multi-source ones until 2020, after which multi-source datasets grow significantly but remain fewer in number.
